overview: Both introduce corrective genetic material, but they differ in whether the change is heritable by future generations.
genZNote: Somatic gene therapy: fixing this patient, this generation only. Germline gene therapy: a change that gets passed down forever after.

aspects.label: Cells Targeted
aspects.valueB: Targets reproductive cells (sperm, egg, or early embryo).

aspects.label: Passed to Offspring?
aspects.valueA: No — the genetic change is not inherited by the patient's children.
aspects.valueB: Yes — the genetic change can be passed on to future generations.

aspects.label: Ethical/Legal Status
aspects.valueA: Widely accepted and practised in approved clinical settings.
aspects.valueB: Highly controversial and banned or heavily restricted in most countries.

overlay.examHighYieldNote: Germline gene editing in humans remains banned or under moratorium in most countries specifically because changes would be passed to all future descendants.
overlay.memoryTrick: Somatic = stops with this person. Germline = carries on to the germline (next generations).
overlay.commonMisconception: All currently approved human gene therapies are somatic — germline gene therapy in humans is not standard clinical practice due to ethical and safety concerns.
